A detailed description of proposed project facilities and structures follows. Engineering details of the proposed facilities are depicted by Figures 1-5, 1-6, and 1-7.
1.4.1 Project Works and Reservoirs
The upper reservoir would be created by a rockfill dam with an impervious core approximately 2,600 feet long and 355 feet high across Bad Creek, a similar type dam approximately 900 feet long and 170 feet high across West Bad Creek, and a saddle dike approximately 900 feet long and 84 feet high across a natural depression on the eastern rim of the reservoir. The crest elevation of the two dams would be at 2,315 feet. Crest elevation of the saddle dike would be at 2,313 feet; the dike would serve as a fuse plug designed to be washed out in the event of overtopping by flood waters or overpumping. The reservoir would have a storage capacity of 33,323 acre-feet, of which 30,228 acre-feet would be usable storage between minimum elevation of 2,150 feet and full pool elevation of 2,310 feet. Maximum drawdown would be 160 feet, and dead storage below elevation 2,150 feet would be 3,095 acre-feet.
The provision of a fuse plug at the upper reservoir would be an emergency measure. The Applicant would provide redundant water level control systems that would prevent the upper reservoir from overtopping by overpumping or flood water. Only an extremely unusual event would cause the fuse plug to wash out.
The intakes, which would be located in the southeast portion of the upper reservoir, would consist of a reinforced concrete structure with 8 ungated openings, 15 feet wide and 12 feet high, with an invert elevation of 2,120 feet. Anticipated maximum flows through the structure would be 13,200 cfs generating and 10,920 cfs pumping.
